primitives.name: Orinq receipts pallet
primitives.desc: Receipt registry with M-of-N committee attestation, availability certification, anchor records, attestor bonds and slashing, and fee escrow — the on-chain truth every other primitive commits to.

primitives.name: MOTRA fee resource
primitives.desc: Non-transferable transaction-fee resource generated from MATRA holdings (NIGHT/DUST model), charged by a signed extension, with sponsor delegation; the extension also gives a runtime-named (signer, call) set the top transaction-pool priority, one slot per signer, so the guardian's veto cannot be outbid for a place in a block.

primitives.name: Billing pallet
primitives.desc: Application-layer MATRA billing (pay_request) for API calls, metering and attestation evidence — the user-facing spend surface, distinct from MOTRA tx fees.

primitives.name: TEE attestation pallet
primitives.desc: Hardware attestation-evidence registry (secp256r1 and ARM TrustZone phone attestors) binding TEE quotes to receipts.

primitives.name: Committee seating gate
primitives.desc: Composed authority-selection gate: input sanitizer, dead-registered and dead-core liveness filters, seat-ramp clamp, live-quorum floor, growth-slack invariant, break-glass floor and pinned-committee override; refuses (keep-current) rather than seat a committee that cannot finalize, so a fresh chain keeps the genesis committee its chain spec declares until a quorum of Cardano's draw has authored. The author and every importing peer judge it on the same state: the runtime's check_inherents initialises the block first. Genesis refuses a chain spec whose committee is empty, has Aura or GRANDPA authorities seeded beside it, has more seats than MaxValidators, lists an authority twice or out of ascending cross-chain-key order, or gives two authorities one Aura or GRANDPA key.

primitives.name: Main-chain follower
primitives.desc: Cardano main-chain follower backends (db-sync and yaci-store with Mithril-certified stake) supplying candidate registrations and the D-parameter to authority selection.

primitives.name: Mainnet launch preflight
primitives.desc: Fail-closed genesis and launch gate: reads the raw chain spec, the runtime metadata extracted from its code, the authority launch commands (opening sh -c wrappers) and each authority's running node argv from a /proc/<pid>/cmdline capture, the nginx and cloudflared RPC proxy configs, each public RPC URL probed live over HTTP and a WebSocket, and Cardano mainnet through Kupo (the cMATRA genesis lock and its datum, and the permissioned candidates datum). Refuses on a well-known key anywhere (genesis, runtime code, any role or multisig member, the Cardano committee, node configs including dev-phrase URIs and the dev seed, the signing key), Sudo.Key or a genesis account no declared role accounts for, Root not a multisig of threshold 2 or more, an undeclared off-chain role, a chain spec the anchor worker would read as a test network, attestor or validator reward parameters that are undeclared or not what genesis and the runtime hold, unsafe RPC on an authority, a public RPC URL that lists a method outside the safe set or answers an unsafe one, an authority with no launch entry, under-endowed attestors, genesis storage outside an allowlist, issuance plus the runtime's emission reserves above what the genesis lock holds, a lock fewer than two key holders can spend or not bound to this genesis, PerpEngine under any name, a runtime override or code substitute, a genesis-enabled Cardano deposit observation with no checkpoint, or genesis, code, chain-spec and launch manifest hashes that differ from a manifest signed by a launch key the repo pins.

primitives.name: Reproducible runtime build
primitives.desc: Builds a commit's runtime blob at a fixed path in a digest-pinned Rust image, with the runtime's build script remapping the toolchain, Cargo home and repository directories its panic messages name, so every builder gets the same bytes and code hash: the code a signed launch manifest pins can be rebuilt from source, and a genesis built from a plain spec carrying it does not depend on the node that ran build-spec.

primitives.name: Root timelock
primitives.desc: Holds every non-exempt Root call for a per-class delay (recovery for committee toggles and delay raises, the standard delay for everything else including consensus-key levers, sudo key rotation and kill-switch restarts unless the guardian co-signs, long for the dedicated bridge and supply levers) in a bounded vetoable queue with a guardian veto, bulk veto, fast-track and a one-shot advance approval that Root runs without a queue place, plus one guardian change the guardian cannot veto and the sudo key can withdraw; the runtime call filter lets the sudo key reach Root at once only for pause, withdrawal and session-bounded finality break-glass calls, for scheduling and for the approved call, each timelock call is charged for every call its classifier walks, and genesis refuses a chain spec without an independent guardian, or with a development account as guardian, and allows an unguarded one only when its sudo key is a development account or absent. The guardian's veto and co-sign calls (cancel, cancel_all, fast_track, approve), signed by the current guardian directly or through a multisig as_multi wrapper, are given the top transaction-pool priority through the MOTRA fee extension, bounded to one slot per signer and to the wrapped call's own weight, so a stolen sudo key cannot buy its way past the veto and a compromised guardian cannot use the priority to fill blocks.
